components.name: Device Action Button
components.description: A compact physical-control button used for random and device actions.
components.css: .ds-device-button { height: 32px; min-width: 96px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; border: 0; border-radius: 4px; background: #2eb85c; color: #fafafa; font-family: ChillMatrixBlack, 'Press Start 2P', cursive; font-size: 8px; box-shadow: inset 2px 2px 4px rgba(255,255,255,0.4), inset -2px -2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.2), 2px 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.2); transition: transform 150ms ease-out, background 150ms ease-out, box-shadow 150ms ease-out; } .ds-device-button:hover { background: #29a653; } .ds-device-button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #8cf2d0; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-device-button:active { transform: translateY(1px); box-shadow: inset 2px 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.2), inset -2px -2px 4px rgba(255,255,255,0.1); }

components.name: Screen Search Input
components.description: The screen-native search field for filtering Pokemon.
components.css: .ds-screen-input { height: 40px; width: 220px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid rgba(140,242,208,0.2); background: #305045; color: #8cf2d0; padding: 8px 12px; font-family: Inter, 'Noto Sans SC', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; transition: border-color 150ms ease-out, box-shadow 150ms ease-out; } .ds-screen-input::placeholder { color: rgba(140,242,208,0.4); } .ds-screen-input:hover { border-color: rgba(140,242,208,0.35); } .ds-screen-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: rgba(140,242,208,0.55); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(140,242,208,0.22); }

components.name: Pokemon Type Badge
components.description: A semantic Pokemon type label using the full-spectrum type palette.
components.css: .ds-type-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 4px; border: 2px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.2); background: #f47b25; color: #fafafa; padding: 4px 8px; font-family: Inter, 'Noto Sans SC', sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; box-shadow: 0 4px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.25); } .ds-type-badge:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #8cf2d0; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Pokemon Cell
components.description: A compact selectable Pokemon grid cell inside the screen.
components.css: .ds-pokemon-cell { position: relative; width: 64px; height: 76px; display: inline-flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 4px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid rgba(140,242,208,0.2); background: #305045; color: #8cf2d0; padding: 6px; transition: transform 200ms ease-out, border-color 200ms ease-out, background 200ms ease-out, box-shadow 200ms ease-out; } .ds-pokemon-cell:hover { background: rgba(140,242,208,0.1); border-color: rgba(140,242,208,0.4); } .ds-pokemon-cell:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgba(140,242,208,0.55); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-pokemon-cell:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-pokemon-id { font-family: ChillMatrixBlack, 'Press Start 2P', cursive; font-size: 8px; color: rgba(140,242,208,0.55); } .ds-pokemon-sprite { width: 40px; height: 40px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 50%; background: rgba(140,242,208,0.1); font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; }

components.name: Language Segmented Control
components.description: A compact two-option language control outside the Pokedex screen.
components.css: .ds-lang-toggle { display: inline-flex; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid #b3bfcc; background: #e7ebef; padding: 2px; } .ds-lang-toggle button { width: 64px; border: 0; border-radius: 4px; padding: 4px 10px; font-family: Inter, 'Noto Sans SC', sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; transition: background 150ms ease-out, color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-lang-active { background: #d61f1f; color: #fafafa; } .ds-lang-button { background: transparent; color: #52667a; } .ds-lang-button:hover { background: #d1d9e0; color: #1b2632; } .ds-lang-toggle button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #d61f1f; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
This system should feel like a handheld Pokedex console: compact, tactile, mechanical, and game-native. The product surface is the red device shell, the deep green screens, the glowing text, the small physical controls, and the dense data panels working together as one usable object.

The visual system is allowed to feel playful, but it must stay task-focused. Mobile users are browsing, filtering, collecting, battling, and building teams; every flourish has to support those jobs. The interface should reject ordinary website composition and preserve the sense that the user is operating a device.
keyCharacteristics: Mobile-first device composition, with the Pokedex shell as the primary surface.
Game-like mechanical controls with crisp state feedback.
Dense information presented inside dark screen panels with phosphor-colored text.
Bilingual typography that balances readable Chinese UI with pixel-label atmosphere.
Motion and shadow used for interaction feedback, not decorative spectacle.

rules.name: The Device First Rule
rules.body: Red belongs to the Pokedex hardware first, not to decorative page sections.

rules.name: The Phosphor Screen Rule
rules.body: Inside screen panels, use Screen Forest plus Phosphor Mint as the default relationship; do not turn the screen into ordinary light-mode UI.

rules.name: The Type Color Rule
rules.body: Full-spectrum colors are reserved for Pokemon type meaning and battle semantics, not random decoration.

rules.name: The Pixel Restraint Rule
rules.body: Pixel fonts are forbidden for dense body text, error details, and long Chinese copy.

rules.name: The No Fluid UI Type Rule
rules.body: Product UI uses fixed rem sizes and breakpoint adjustments; do not scale text with viewport width.

rules.name: The Mechanical Feedback Rule
rules.body: Buttons and inputs should feel like physical controls with crisp feedback. Use pressed states, small translate transforms, and focus rings.

rules.name: The Screen Flatness Rule
rules.body: Pokemon cells, stats, lists, and filters inside screens should not float as cards. Use borders and tonal states instead.

dos: Do keep the Pokedex shell as the product surface, with red hardware and green screen panels carrying the experience.
Do prioritize mobile touch ergonomics: compact but reachable buttons, stable screen heights, and clear selected states.
Do use Phosphor Mint for screen text and selected state, not generic black-on-white content inside the device.
Do reserve Pokemon type colors for semantic type, battle, and team information.
Do make buttons and inputs feel like physical controls with fast, crisp feedback.
Do keep bilingual Chinese and English text readable by using Inter and Noto Sans SC for real content.
donts: Don't make this feel like a marketing landing page, SaaS dashboard, generic content site, blog, or decorative fan page.
Don't wrap ordinary website UI in Pokemon colors and call it a Pokedex.
Don't add oversized hero sections, feature explanations, or desktop-first compositions around the device.
Don't use pixel fonts for body copy, dense stats, forms, or long Chinese text.
Don't turn screen panels into floating card grids. Use tonal layers, borders, and compact controls.
Don't use side-stripe borders, gradient text, decorative glassmorphism, hero metrics, or repeated identical icon-card grids.
